newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- FX vols softer despite dollar gyrations.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- FX vols softer despite dollar gyrations.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were a touch softer in late U.S. business even though the dollar gyrated in relatively wide ranges above recent resistance levels, dealers said.
They noted that curve-flattening seemed to be the name of the game today as many in the market viewed the volatility curve in most currency pairs to be too steep.

"We're seeing fresh two-way interest in trading and a lot of calendar interest in the last couple of days," said a trader at a European bank in Chicago. "It seems like the stuff is being offered all along the curve, though."
"Although we are seeing a pretty good movement in spot, it's been a tight market volatility-wise," agreed Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior trader at Bank of Yokohama in New York. "It's been very technical."
One-month implied volatilities for dollar/mark and dollar/yen stood at 6.65/6.95 and 6.6/6.9 percent respectively late in the U.S., marginally off late Wednesday levels.

The spot dollar rose above 1.5250 marks in the U.S., helped by the mark's continued weakness against European currencies -- notably the lira. The mark fell through the 1000-lira psychological barrier towards 995.
The greenback also rose above 110.70 yen and was eyeing its July 8 high of 111.20, traders said.

"A lot of people have been viewing 111.20 as a significant top, so I'd expect them to cover short strikes up there as we approach that level," Hiramatsu said. "But until we get there, I don't think there would be an aggressive one-way trade."
Despite the dollar's rise, risk reversals, which measure pricing differentials between puts and calls, were little changed.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal for dollar/mark was around par.
One-month 25-delta for dollar/yen stood at 0.2/0.6 percent in favor of yen calls.
Hiramatsu said Japanese corporations were still keen on buying low-delta yen calls whenever they become cheap.
In European currencies, dollar/Swiss franc volatilities remained high in nervous trading, with one-month at about 8.2/8.6 percent, as the dollar hurdled above 1.25 francs.
One-month mark/lira volatility was off overnight highs at 4.9/5.3 percent.
